scope: Three flows of the service, about ten operations: same-currency ledger summary (F1), archive constraints and their effect on the summary (F2), isolation between two users (F3).
how_to_read: Each rule states what the service must do. A rule is judged only by comparing observed responses with its statement; the statement is never to be adjusted so that a failing response passes.

rules.title: Totals per currency, never mixed
rules.statement: In ledger.summary, by_currency[C] sums only the holdings and transactions whose currency is C. `base` equals by_currency[base_currency]. excluded_currencies lists every other key of by_currency, in ascending order. No amount of one currency is ever added to another.
rules.owner_confirm: A currency appears in by_currency only if the user has a holding in it or a transaction in it within the requested month; the base currency always appears.

rules.title: Assets come from holdings
rules.statement: total_assets_minor = cash_balance_minor + holdings_value_minor. Holdings of asset_type cash count toward cash_balance_minor, all other holdings toward holdings_value_minor (and holdings_cost_minor). Transactions never change assets. Assets are current values and do not depend on `month`.
rules.source: docs: API.md section 2 and the 2026-09-05 ledger snapshot note; owner test: transactions do not mutate cash snapshots

rules.title: Holding valuation
rules.statement: market_value_minor = quantity x unit price, rounded half up to the minor unit. The unit price is current_price, else average_cost, else 0; cash without a price has unit price 1. cost_minor = quantity x average_cost (1 for cash, 0 for other holdings without average_cost). unrealized_profit_minor = market_value_minor - cost_minor, and is null (not 0) when average_cost is missing. valuation_status is priced when a price is known, otherwise estimated.
rules.source: docs: API.md ledger snapshot note (cost-based estimate, null profit without cost)
rules.owner_confirm: Half-up rounding; unit price 0 when both price and cost are missing.

rules.title: Monthly income and expense
rules.statement: For transactions whose occurred_at falls in the requested month: income_minor is the sum of the absolute amounts of DEPOSIT, DIVIDEND and INTEREST; expense_minor is the sum of the absolute amounts of WITHDRAWAL and FEE. BUY, SELL, TRANSFER and OTHER are neither income nor expense. net_cashflow_minor = income_minor - expense_minor.
rules.owner_confirm: Which types count as income and which as expense (the documentation only says the month filters the transaction figures).

rules.title: Transfers stay within one currency
rules.statement: A TRANSFER needs both account_id and to_account_id. If the two accounts have different currencies the request fails with HTTP 400 and code TRANSFER_CURRENCY_MISMATCH, and nothing from that batch is saved.

rules.title: Malformed transfers are rejected
rules.statement: A TRANSFER whose to_account_id equals its account_id, and any non-TRANSFER transaction that carries a to_account_id, is rejected with HTTP 400 and code VALIDATION_ERROR.
rules.owner_confirm: Both rejections and the VALIDATION_ERROR code.

rules.title: Month format
rules.statement: `month` must match YYYY-MM with a month from 01 to 12; anything else is HTTP 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR. Behaviour without `month` is not judged.
rules.source: docs: API.md section 2 and the OpenAPI pattern

rules.title: Batches are all or nothing
rules.statement: holdings.batch_upsert and transactions.batch_upsert save every item or none. If any item fails (validation, missing reference, outdated version) the whole batch is rolled back and existing data is unchanged.

rules.title: Replaying a batch does not duplicate
rules.statement: Sending the same client_request_id with identical content again returns the first response and creates no new records, as long as everything the request refers to is still active.
rules.owner_confirm: Replay returns the stored first response. Reusing the id with different content, and replays after a referenced record was archived, are not judged.

rules.title: Soft archive
rules.statement: After a successful archive (HTTP 200) the record's version increases by 1 and the record is gone from its list endpoint and from ledger.summary: archiving a transaction lowers income or expense of its month, archiving a holding lowers its share of cash_balance_minor or holdings_value_minor, holdings_cost_minor and total_assets_minor. Nothing else changes.

rules.title: Archiving needs the current version
rules.statement: An archive request whose version differs from the record's current version fails with HTTP 409 and code VERSION_CONFLICT, and the record stays active.
rules.source: docs: API.md (409 means conflict of state or version)

rules.title: Accounts with dependants cannot be archived
rules.statement: An account that still has active holdings cannot be archived (HTTP 409, ACCOUNT_HAS_HOLDINGS). An account that still has active transactions, as source or as transfer target, cannot be archived (HTTP 409, ACCOUNT_HAS_TRANSACTIONS). If both apply, ACCOUNT_HAS_HOLDINGS is returned. A rejected archive leaves the account active. Once the dependants are archived, the account can be archived.
rules.owner_confirm: The guard, the two codes and the precedence.

rules.title: Holdings with transactions cannot be archived
rules.statement: A holding that is referenced (holding_id) by an active transaction cannot be archived (HTTP 409, HOLDING_HAS_TRANSACTIONS). After those transactions are archived it can be.

rules.title: Archived or unknown records do not exist
rules.statement: Archiving a record that is already archived, or whose id does not exist, fails with HTTP 404 and code NOT_FOUND and changes nothing. Creating a transaction or holding in an archived account is rejected as not found.
rules.source: docs: API.md (404 means the single resource does not exist)

rules.title: Lists and summaries are private
rules.statement: A user's account, holding and transaction lists and ledger.summary contain only that user's records. Writes, updates and archives by user A never change what user B reads, and the other way round.

rules.title: Another user's ids are not usable
rules.statement: Updating or archiving a record with an id that belongs to another user fails with HTTP 404 and code NOT_FOUND, exactly as for an id that does not exist (same code and message), and the owner's data is unchanged.
rules.source: docs: API.md (404) and the service's own message for unknown or foreign records

rules.title: Another user's accounts cannot be referenced
rules.statement: Creating a holding or transaction whose account_id or to_account_id belongs to another user fails with HTTP 404 and code NOT_FOUND, and nothing is saved.

rules.title: Authentication is required
rules.statement: Without a token every in-scope operation returns HTTP 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED; with an invalid token HTTP 401 with code TOKEN_INVALID. No user data is returned.
